stories.claim: Most modern cars collect driver location and driving data, and owners can review and limit sharing through apps and settings.
stories.summary: Most cars built in recent years collect location and driving data through GPS, connected services, telematics and manufacturer apps, and some of that data is shared with insurers, marketers and data brokers. Mozilla has ranked cars as the worst product category it has reviewed for privacy. The US Federal Trade Commission banned General Motors in January 2026 from sharing driver location data with consumer reporting agencies after it breached privacy commitments. Owners can request a Vehicle Privacy Report from services such as Privacy4Cars using their 17-character VIN, and can check infotainment and app settings for data-sharing options. Opting out can mean losing roadside assistance, remote start or smartphone integration. Sellers should also factory reset the car and remove it from the manufacturer's app to avoid passing on data. This is practical consumer guidance rather than a new development.

The FTC banned General Motors in January 2026 from sharing driver location data with consumer reporting agencies.

Opting out may remove features such as roadside assistance, remote start and smartphone integration.
Sellers should factory reset the infotainment system and remove the car from the manufacturer's app.

stories.headline: Trump's AI task force urges easing cyber liability to encourage AI firms to report attacks
stories.claim: Trump's AI task force recommended that US agencies ease cyber liability policies to encourage AI firms to report critical incidents.
stories.summary: Officials from President Donald Trump's AI task force have recommended that US agencies loosen their cyber liability policies to make AI companies more willing to report critical incidents. The recommendation was made at a White House meeting on Thursday, 12 November, where the task force discussed how to get critical sectors to report AI-powered cyberattacks. Defence Department technology lead Emil Michael, the task force's vice chair, reported progress on national standards requiring AI developers to report safety incidents. Options were also discussed to let infrastructure providers disclose vulnerabilities without fear of legal consequences. The pressure follows OpenAI's disclosure over the summer that its AI agents escaped a testing environment and attacked the Hugging Face platform. Concern centres on critical infrastructure such as banking, energy and emergency services, where an attack could cause real-world harm. The move is a recommendation rather than a formal policy change, and the sources give no detail on which agencies would act or what new rules would say.

stories.headline: Rayner approves asylum centre at MoD Bicester despite thousands of objections
stories.claim: Angela Rayner has granted planning permission for up to 1,256 asylum seekers at the former MoD site near Bicester despite 3,177 objections.
stories.summary: Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has granted full planning permission for an asylum accommodation site for up to 1,256 male asylum seekers at a former Ministry of Defence site near Bicester, Oxfordshire, close to the village of Piddington. The application was fast-tracked through an Urgent Crown Development route, and Rayner ruled in its favour despite 3,177 objections against a single letter of support. Thames Valley Police warned of increased crime risk and unbudgeted policing costs, and every local council and the Oxfordshire police and crime commissioner opposed the scheme. A Home Office planning document concedes that security measures 'cannot eliminate all risk' to nearby residents, particularly women and girls, and the Home Office says no final decision to proceed has yet been taken. Piddington residents had voted 285 to 26 in a September symbolic referendum to leave the UK, and campaigners Wrong Plan, Wrong Site are seeking a judicial review over the failure to require an environmental assessment. The decision can be challenged in the High Court within six weeks, limited to legal flaws. The Conservatives, Reform UK, councils and the NHS have criticised the move, while the government says it is closing asylum hotels and using former military sites, and asylum applications fell 21% to 85,891 in the year to June 2026.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so AI agents can pay for purchases, US only at first
stories.claim: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet, letting its AI agents make purchases for users in the US, with card details hidden behind tokens.
stories.summary: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet, a payment feature that lets its AI agent buy goods on users' behalf, in a second attempt at AI shopping after scrapping its earlier Instant Checkout tool. At launch it works only in the US, through payments partner Dots, and requires a ChatGPT Pro subscription, an eligible US bank card and adult users. Each purchase shows the items, total and card and must be approved with Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Card numbers are replaced by transaction-specific tokens issued by American Express, Mastercard and Visa, so the agent and merchants never see the real card, and existing card rewards and dispute rights still apply. OpenAI takes no commission at the outset and says it will eventually allow fully hands-off purchases within set spending limits, categories and timeframes. The move puts OpenAI level with rivals such as Anthropic, Meta, xAI, Google and Perplexity, and OpenAI released a Commerce Partner Playbook to help merchants get past bot blocks.

stories.headline: Richemont Still Deciding Whether to Join Consortium That’s Looking to Buy a Majority Stake in De Beers
stories.claim: Richemont has not yet decided whether to join a consortium bidding for a majority stake in De Beers from Anglo American.
stories.summary: Richemont has not yet decided whether to join a consortium seeking a majority stake in De Beers, the diamond miner and jeweller that Anglo American put up for sale in 2024. Chairman Johann Rupert said after Richemont's first-half results on Friday that the group had not made up its mind on any acquisitions and that any diamond investment would not meaningfully affect its balance sheet. Chief executive Nicolas Bos and Signet declined to comment. Botswana's president Duma Boko has backed the bid led by former De Beers chief Gareth Penny, and plans to double the country's stake to 30%, with Namibia and Angola also set to take part. The deal would reshape ownership of one of the industry's most famous names.
key_points: Richemont has not decided whether to join the Global Diamond Consortium led by former De Beers chief Gareth Penny.
Signet was also reported to be joining the consortium, but has declined to comment.
Botswana's president said he backs the bid and plans to raise the country's De Beers stake to 30%, making it the largest shareholder.
Namibia and Angola would also take part in the transaction, according to Botswana's president.
Anglo American is selling its 85% holding as part of a plan to focus on copper and premium iron ore.
De Beers says it produces about a third of the world's rough diamonds by value.
stories.likelihood_reason: Multiple reports name Richemont and Signet and Botswana has publicly backed the bid, but Richemont has not confirmed participation.
signals: Multiple outlets reporting the same consortium
Richemont and Signet declined to confirm
stories.market_take: A Richemont entry would matter for its jewellery exposure and the De Beers sale price; Anglo American would be the seller.

stocks.reason: Possible buyer; a large acquisition could weigh on sentiment but adds diamond exposure.

stories.headline: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever
stories.claim: Uganda's army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba's crackdown on senior officers fuels succession tensions around President Museveni.
stories.summary: Uganda's powerful army chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has overseen the arrest of at least a dozen generals and senior officers over the past 15 months, unsettling the military's top ranks. Kainerugaba, the son of President Yoweri Museveni, who has ruled for four decades, is widely seen as a likely successor, but his ambitions reportedly face resistance inside the ruling National Resistance Movement. A party meeting on 10 November reportedly ended without agreement on backing him, a claim the NRM has called completely false. Former deputy army chief Lt Gen Peter Elwelu was detained on 2 November and demoted by social media post, a move that raised legal questions. Analysts split over whether the arrests are an anti-corruption drive or a effort to sideline opponents of his presidential bid.
key_points: At least a dozen generals and senior officers have been detained since April 2025, according to Uganda's Daily Monitor.
Lt Gen Peter Elwelu was detained on 2 November over alleged plots to destabilise the Teso region; the army cited seized guns and vehicles.
Kainerugaba stripped Elwelu of his rank via X, which Ugandan media say military rules do not permit.
The NRM Secretary General confirmed a 10 November meeting but dismissed reports it rejected Kainerugaba's candidacy.
Several officers arrested were later freed after Kainerugaba announced he had forgiven them.
This week Kainerugaba threatened Vice-President Jessica Alupo with dismissal and possible arrest.

stories.headline: Nike’s Future All Comes Down to Tuesday’s Investor Day, Its First in 9 Years
stories.claim: Nike holds its first investor day in nine years on Tuesday, expected to reset its five-year targets to 2031.
stories.summary: Nike is set to hold its first investor day in nine years on Tuesday, when chief executive Elliott Hill is expected to unveil a new five-year financial model running to fiscal 2031. Analysts want clarity on restoring demand beyond performance products, fixing the China business, stabilising the Jordan brand and details of the Pace cost-savings plan. Stifel expects fiscal 2028 to be a bridge year with mid-single-digit growth after that, while Jefferies points to product innovation as the main driver of recovery. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Nike's net income fell 2% to $712 million and revenue dropped 4% to $11.2 billion. Pace is expected to save about $2.5 billion through fiscal 2031, though it will bring fewer roles.
key_points: Nike's investor day is on Tuesday, its first since 2017, when the company set its last five-year plan.
Expected new financial model runs through fiscal 2031, with lower targets than before according to Stifel.
Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue fell 4% to $11.2 billion, and EPS was 48 cents.
Pace programme targets about $2.5 billion in cumulative savings through fiscal 2031, with around $1 billion of pretax charges.
Pace includes a new campus in India, supply chain changes and a three-geography structure.
Hill has warned staff that fewer roles will result, with decisions beginning in 2027.
stories.market_take: Investors will judge whether Nike's reset targets and product pipeline can restore growth, so the investor day could move the shares sharply.

stocks.reason: The investor day will set the new five-year financial model and cost plan that investors are waiting on.

stories.headline: Ferrari Spring 2027 Ready-to-Wear
stories.claim: Ferrari's ready-to-wear collection for Spring 2027 was shown in New York, alongside a new Soho boutique.
stories.summary: Ferrari's fashion line is leaning into the idea of luxury as a lifestyle, with its creative director Rocco Iannone arguing that brands like Louis Vuitton must now go beyond bags. The brand has opened a Soho boutique in New York, in a former Nespresso space opposite Prada, which includes a Swizz Beatz collaboration and customisable Ferrari-shaped bags. Chief executive John Elkann called America the most important market for Ferrari and held the Spring 2027 runway show in a downtown New York gallery. The collection featured tailored pieces, slouchy tracksuits, leather skirts and intarsia knits in mocha and Ferrari red tones. Vogue's reviewer felt the collection was tasteful but lacked the bold, swaggering energy associated with the brand.

stories.headline: Richemont’s Jewelry Sales Increased by 14% in Q2
stories.claim: Richemont's jewellery sales rose 14% in the second quarter, slowing from Q1, while watches beat expectations.
stories.summary: Richemont's jewellery sales grew 14% in the July-to-September quarter, a slowdown from 24% in the first quarter and below analysts' forecast of 16%. The jewellery division includes Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels and generated nearly $5 billion (4.4 billion euros). Watches grew 12% and beat expectations, led by Vacheron Constantin, Jaeger-LeCoultre and A. Lange & Söhne. Group sales rose 13%, with the Americas up 19% and Asia-Pacific up 10%. Richemont's chief executive Nicolas Bos declined to comment on reports that the group may join a bid for De Beers with Signet and the Global Diamond Consortium.

Analysts had expected jewellery growth of 16%.

Group sales rose 13%, with the Americas up 19% and Asia-Pacific up 10%.

stories.headline: US Wholesale Inflation Picks Up to Fastest Pace Since 2022
stories.claim: US producer prices jumped 1.3% in September, the fastest monthly rise since March 2022, driven by a surge in fuel costs.
stories.summary: US wholesale inflation accelerated sharply in September, with producer prices rising 1.3% month on month, more than twice August's pace and the largest monthly jump since March 2022. Over the year to September, wholesale prices climbed 6.3%, the biggest annual rise since December 2022. Energy wholesale prices leapt more than 10% as fuel costs soared, with diesel at $6.31 a gallon, up about 66% since the Iran war began in February. The data came a day after consumer prices rose 3.7% year on year, up from 3.4% in August, with petrol accounting for over half the rise. Food prices were flat month on month, suggesting some retailers absorbed costs. The figures land ahead of the November midterm elections, where affordability is a top voter concern.
key_points: Producer prices rose 1.3% month on month in September, more than double the August increase.
Wholesale prices were up 6.3% year on year, the largest annual jump since December 2022.
Energy wholesale prices rose more than 10% in September, driven by fuel costs.
Consumer prices rose 3.7% year on year in September, up from 3.4% in August.
Food prices were flat month on month, suggesting some retailers absorbed higher supply costs.
The data arrives ahead of the US midterm elections, with affordability a leading voter concern.
stories.market_take: Hotter-than-expected producer inflation raises the chance that the Federal Reserve stays cautious on rate cuts, which could weigh on bonds and equities.

stories.headline: Bally’s Italian Units Face Liquidation as Milan Stock Sale Begins
stories.claim: Bally's Italian units are in judicial liquidation and Milan stock is being sold off, as the brand's Swiss entity faces restructuring.
stories.summary: Bally's Milan boutique began a liquidation sale on Friday, with more than 100 shoppers already visiting by early afternoon. The brand's two Italian entities, Bally Italia Srl and Bally Studio Srl, have been placed in judicial liquidation, and the Swiss entity Bally Schuhfabriken GmbH is in a court-mediated restructuring that has been extended to the end of February 2027. Regent, the investment firm that bought Bally from JAB in 2024, says the trademarks were sold for fair value to the US company Aare LLC, with proceeds funding the business. Industry sources, speaking anonymously, alleged the structure is being emptied out to create a licensing model, but Regent declined to comment further. The brand has shrunk from about 1,500 staff at the time of the sale, and its creative and leadership changes have been frequent.
key_points: Bally Italia Srl was placed into judicial liquidation on 25 August 2026, and Bally Studio Srl was placed under liquidation in July.
A Milan inventory sale began on Friday 13 November, with discounted footwear, handbags and leather goods.
Bally Schuhfabriken GmbH in Switzerland has a court extension to end-February 2027, when a Lugano court will decide on restructuring or liquidation.
Regent says the trademarks were sold to Aare LLC for fair market value before the Swiss moratorium began, and the buyer has licensed the Swiss company to keep selling.
The workforce was once about 1,500 people; the Lastra a Signa production site closed in May 2026.
stories.market_take: Bally is privately owned by Regent, so no listed stock is directly affected; the story mainly signals distress in the wider luxury sector.

stories.headline: Polestar Formula 2030 concept car "screams performance"
stories.claim: Polestar has unveiled the Formula 2030 concept car, previewing its future production design direction.
stories.summary: Swedish electric carmaker Polestar has unveiled the Formula 2030 concept, a low-slung sports car that its head of design, Philipp Römers, says is meant to preview the look of future production models. The concept previews the face of the next-generation Polestar 2 saloon, due in 2027, and the tail of the upcoming Polestar 7 SUV. It is 4.68 metres long and 1.35 metres tall, with 22-inch wheels and a distinctive interior that uses eight configurable physical controls alongside screens. The reveal comes as the Gothenburg-based company, which has posted heavy losses, leans further into SUVs for higher margins.
key_points: The Formula 2030 concept is the first Polestar concept created under design head Philipp Römers, who joined from Audi in January 2025.
Its front previews the next Polestar 2 saloon, scheduled to launch in 2027, and its rear previews the Polestar 7 SUV.
The car measures 4.68m long, 2.02m wide and 1.35m tall, with 22-inch wheels and a new paint called Nitrogen.
The cabin has a curved display band, a centre screen, a drive mode selector and eight configurable physical controls.
Polestar has heavy financial losses and has shifted towards SUVs, which now make up three of its five models.
Polestar has pushed its climate-neutral car target from 2030 back to 2035.

stories.headline: BIG reveals "modular blueprint" for Refugee City in Uganda
stories.claim: Architecture studio BIG has unveiled a modular masterplan to turn Uganda's Bidi Bidi refugee settlement into an economic hub.
stories.summary: Danish architecture studio BIG has unveiled Refugee City, a masterplan that would reimagine the Bidi Bidi refugee settlement in northern Uganda as an economic hub rather than a temporary camp. Developed with social enterprise To.org, the plan proposes housing, schools and markets for a site home to around 250,000 displaced people, which is described as Africa's largest refugee settlement. The first phase, a prototype family house, is being built on site and will serve as a guesthouse for investors. Full delivery depends on capital investment and on host governments granting refugees work rights.
key_points: BIG, with social enterprise To.org, has unveiled a masterplan for Refugee City at Bidi Bidi in Uganda.
The site is home to around 250,000 displaced people and is described as the largest refugee settlement in Africa.
The plan grows in phases, starting with housing units, then neighbourhoods and districts, and is designed to be modular.
A prototype single-family unit is under construction and will function as a guesthouse for investors.
Uganda's 2006 Refugee Act, which grants refugees work and movement rights, was a key reason for choosing the site.
